summary.name: Logit.io Blog
summary.one_liner: The blog of Logit.io, a hosted log management and observability service built around Elastic Stack / OpenSearch, publishing setup guides, tutorials and product announcements.
use_cases: ship logs from servers, Kubernetes or Windows hosts to a hosted OpenSearch stack
set up OpenTelemetry logs, traces and metrics
migrate from Splunk, Datadog or self-managed ELK
tune OpenSearch shards, ingestion and retention
query production logs from Cursor or Claude via MCP
summary.what_it_does: The page is the index of Logit.io's blog, listing roughly 60 posts, most dated 2026, with a few older 2025 industry monitoring guides. Recent posts are practical how-tos covering Filebeat, Fluent Bit, Winlogbeat, Elastic Agent, Wazuh, OpenTelemetry collectors and SDKs, and Logstash/OpenSearch troubleshooting such as 429 bulk rejections and mapping conflicts. It also covers Logit.io-specific features like the hosted OTLP endpoint, the hosted read-only OpenSearch MCP endpoint, the Dashboard Library, data residency settings and the developer API. Several posts compare or give migration guidance from Splunk, Datadog and self-managed ELK.
notable: Hosted OpenSearch and Elastic Stack-based log stacks with managed Logstash and OpenSearch Dashboards
Hosted read-only OpenSearch MCP endpoint for querying logs from Cursor or Claude
Hosted OTLP endpoint accepting logs, traces and metrics
Account-level EU and UK data residency for Hosted OpenSearch
caveats: Pricing details are not stated on the blog index; several posts mention per-node pricing but the figures are not on this page
Older 2025 posts are generic industry monitoring guides rather than Logit.io product documentation
Data residency regions are locked to the first stack on an account, per the residency post listings
